newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin says can outbid BA for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: Virgin says can outbid BA for Air Liberte.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline said on Tuesday it would present a bid for ailing carrier Air Liberte topping that of rival British Airways Plc (BA) -- if a French court agreed to wait for it.

"There are components of our offer that will make it more attractive for all parties concerned. Clearly, I think our bid is better," Virgin Express's chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters by telephone.
"I'm hoping they (the court) will wait for us, to give us the time we need to make a presentable offer," he said. Virgin planned to submit its bid later this week.
Air Liberte, which has a 12 percent share of the French domestic market, filed for receivership at the Creteil commercial court on September 26.
A number of other parties would be involved in Virgin's bid, Ornstein said. He declined to name them. "It's just a question of getting everybody to agree on the formula."
Airline sources said Virgin Express was holding talks with French state-owned carrier Air France on plans to cooperate on the Air Liberte bid.
BA and its French subsidiary TAT said on Monday they filed their plan to take over Air Liberte in conjunction with French Banque Rivaud and expected a court decision on Wednesday.
Ornstein believed Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines, had more time for its bid to the court-appointed administrator of Air Liberte.
"Our advisors have been in contact (with the court) through intermediaries, so I hope (they will wait for us)," he said.
"Certainly we have to do something quickly, no question about that. But my advisors tell me that we have time," he said.
BA and Rivaud have made a 780 million French franc ($151.8 million) bid for Air Liberte.
Ornstein said the offer had been delayed by a commercial deal, signed last Friday, with Belgian national airline Sabena for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow.

That deal gives Virgin Express access to coveted take-off and landing slots at Heathrow and enables it to offer connections via Brussels between London and seven continental European cities served by Virgin Express.
"When we have special projects like the Sabena transaction that obviously takes up a lot of time," Ornstein said.
He declined to give details on the bid but added Virgin held a planning session with its investment bankers on Monday and had been working on the bid last weekend.
He said the bid was not based on the assumption that Air Liberte would be liquidated first but was "more along the lines of continuation of the business".
